# Kathinabheda (Pvr 16)

**ID:** Pvr 16
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Kathinabheda
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul12.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kathinabheda* ("The robe-making ceremony", Parivāra 16) provides a detailed summary and analytical breakdown of the monastic procedures governing the *kaṭhina* cloth. The text sets out the formal regulations for making and dedicating the cloth, enumerating twenty-four improper methods and seventeen proper methods of formally making robes, while presenting catechisms regarding who is eligible or disqualified from carrying out the rite [Horner 1966]. In addition to the translation by I.B. Horner in *The Book of the Discipline*, a modern English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner 1966].

In the traditional manuscript ordering evaluated by I.B. Horner and Oskar von Hinüber, the text appears as chapter fourteen of the *Parivāra* [von Hinüber 1996; Horner 1966]. Von Hinüber notes that some manuscripts mark a clear textual boundary at the conclusion of the chapter, followed by a noticeable stylistic break before the *Upālipañcaka* (which resembles a *Khandhaka* text), raising the question of whether *Kathinabheda* constituted an earlier conclusion to the *Parivāra* collection [von Hinüber 1996].

According to DharmaNexus text-reuse analysis, *Kathinabheda* shares significant textual material within the Pali canon with the *Kathinakkhandhaka* (Kd 7) and numerous treatises of the *Paṭṭhāna* (notably the *Piṭṭhiduka*, *Kilesagocchaka*, *Saññojanagocchaka*, and *Cūḷantaraduka*), as well as internal *Parivāra* texts (*Adhikaraṇabheda* and *Upālipañcaka*) and the commentary *Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with Sanskrit material in the *Kaṭhināvadāna* and with Tibetan Vinaya texts, particularly the *Vinayavastu* (D0001 / D0001-3), *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105), *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2), and *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122) [DharmaNexus].
